ab_provenance: environment.json diff between runs: only MODEL/MODEL_DIR and scope UUID differ

verdicts.budgets: Both runs: cgroup peak ~32.40 GiB <= 40 GiB (MemoryMax 36G), VRAM peak 18.63/22.67 GiB <= 28 GiB, zero max/oom/oom_kill events, swap <= 0.52 GiB.
verdicts.goal_20_tok_s: Second (warm) request of each run: ps-iq2xxs 50.19, reference 44.33 tok/s — both >= 20 within budgets. First (cold) requests: 31.50 / 21.86 tok/s — also >= 20.
verdicts.ab_delta: Warm decode ps-iq2xxs 50.19 vs reference 44.33 tok/s (+13%); cold 31.50 vs 21.86 (+44%). Same acceptance regime (~0.67). Not a multi-seed/multi-prompt study: n=1 prompt, n=2 requests per arm.
verdicts.host_state_confound: HISTORICAL runs of the same reference config measured 6.48/8.49 tok/s (2026-09-06) and 8.37/10.88 (2026-09-06 reverse order). Today both checkpoints are 2.6-6.7x faster than the historical reference numbers under an identical harness. Today's host state: MemAvailable 40.6-48.6 GiB at guard, swap 0.25-0.52 GiB during runs vs historical 1.2-2.2 GiB swap and 42-46 GiB MemAvailable. The speed difference vs history is therefore dominated by host memory state (page cache/swap), not by code. The same-day A/B (both arms today, minutes apart) is the only clean comparison; the PS checkpoint's win is real but modest (+13% warm).
verdicts.not_proven: Sustained throughput at depth/long decode, 64K/264K context, quality parity of IQ2_XXS vs Q4_K_M, tool-calling correctness, Hermes end-to-end. Cold-start latency of the 75 GB file on a truly cold page cache is NOT measured (page cache was warm from a previous download).

next_steps: Repeat A/B with 2x512 or 2x1024 tokens to check sustained decode beyond warm-up.
IQ2_XXS quality gate: tool-calling JSON correctness + needle-recall before any default switch (community claims unverified).
Re-run A/B after a controlled cold cache (posix_fadvise DONTNEED on the model files) to bound worst-case first-token latency.
